title: OOD
body:
**Object Oriented Design.** Turn the domain objects that [[OOA]] found into classes that can
actually be built: decide each class's [[Interface]], its [[Implementation]], what it hides
([[Encapsulation]]), and what inherits from what.

For the OOA/OOD/OOM distinction, see [[OOA]]; it holds the table so all three notes agree.
The short version is that analysis is about the problem and design is about the solution, so
this is the stage where classes appear that have no counterpart in the real world.

What gets decided here:

- **Responsibilities.** One class, one job. That is [[Coupling and Cohesion]] stated as a
  design rule, and it is the thing most [[Code Smells]] are a violation of.
- **Interfaces.** What each class exposes, which fixes how much the rest of the system can
  depend on it. Depending on an [[Interface]] rather than an [[Implementation]] is what keeps
  coupling low.
- **Hierarchies.** Where [[Inheritance]] genuinely applies (a real *is-a*) and where it is
  being used to share code between things that are not related, which is the usual way an
  inheritance tree goes wrong.
- **[[Polymorphism]] points.** Where the system needs to add a new variant later without
  changing existing code.

Belongs to the [[Design]] phase of the [[SDLC]]. Drawn with [[OOM]]; implemented in
[[Java]] in [[INFORMATION STRUCTURES]].
